bio: A short distance from Parque Vicente López y Planes, in the heart of Recoleta, this restaurant occupies an elegant 20th-century mansion that served as an art gallery for many years (taking its name, as a tribute). The restaurant, headed up by Italian chef Sebastián Raggiante (also at the helm of the successful Raggio Osteria) and managed on a day-to-day basis by chef Nicolás Raimundo, features a dining room with two distinct areas and an à la carte service (complemented by a more affordable set lunch menu) where you’ll find antipasti, fresh homemade pasta (we were particularly impressed by their Orecchiette with Neapolitan ragù), risottos made exclusively with Carnaroli rice (for a minimum of two people), as well as a selection of meat and fish dishes, such as their Saltimbocca alla romana with buttered potato purée and thyme. Fun fact: There are numerous Italian products for sale on enticing shelves at the entrance: pasta, sauces, Campari... and several Argentine wines.
